findings.note: dump.cs declares MasterActivate/MasterDeactivate/TriggerEnemyWave as private; the interop assembly exposes all three as public methods, so a binding can call them. This is the one place where the interop surface is wider than the dump's own visibility, and it is why the alarm row is implemented at all.

nativeEntries.meaning: the door's own interaction entry, called with onlyUnlock=false. It toggles, so the door's own LastStatus is read first and an open or opening door is left alone with `door-already-open`. Address and body shape are the rows already frozen in door-terminal-hooks.json members[door-status/door-type]; this slice read no bytes of its own.

the one entry the game itself uses to open a door whose own lock or interaction gate would refuse; it is the only policy value that ignores those conditions, so `respect` and `force` are the two real behaviours and no third one is offered.

refusals.meaning: the door's own eDoorStatus and its own InteractionAllowed property refused before anything was written; the pre-write reads are the same ones DoorObservation uses, so a refusal here and a published state can never describe two different doors.

no member on either entry takes a caller-set animation duration, and the catalog's `duration` port is declared optional here so a plan stays loadable; a non-zero value is refused by name instead of being reported as honoured.

nativeEntries.meaning: the same toggling entry, asked only for a door that reads open or opening so a second close cannot open it.

refusals.meaning: the interaction entry carries no occupancy decision, so `crush` is refused rather than run as a plain close and reported as the requested one.
the interaction entry has no force form; the door's own force entry is an open, not a close, so `force` on a close is refused by name.

nativeEntries.meaning: the alarm this door owns. The level creates it in LG_SecurityDoor.SetupChainedPuzzleLock (0x15A4500), whose frozen edges call ChainedPuzzleManager.CreatePuzzleInstance (0x1736F50) and ChainedPuzzleInstance.add_OnPuzzleSolved (0x17368B0); objective-hooks.json's edge `door-locks-setup-for-puzzle.calls-solved-callback` (from 0x15A02A0, the lock component's own SetupForChainedPuzzle body) subscribes to the same callback. The getter's RVA is a shared stub, so it is callable but not a Harmony target by address; this action only calls it.

the lock component's own statement that its chained puzzle is an alarm. It is the gate that keeps a door locked with a scan or with anything else from being started as an alarm. Read by reflection only: no dump line and no body were inspected for it.

mode=start. objective-hooks.json freezes the verified edge MasterActivate -> TriggerEnemyWave (0x1736600), and TriggerEnemyWave -> Mastermind's own survival-wave entry, so activating the puzzle is what starts the alarm's wave.
mode=stop, the native stop side of the same alarm/scan instance.
the readback the mode is applied against: an active puzzle is not re-activated and an inactive one is not deactivated, and that decision is reported as an already-in-state commit rather than a write.

refusals.meaning: a door with no lock component holds neither an alarm flag nor a puzzle.
the lock component's own m_hasAlarm is false: its puzzle is a scan or another lock kind, and this row is the alarm row.
m_hasAlarm is true but the puzzle instance did not read, so there is nothing to activate or deactivate.

a plan supplied the catalog's `alarm` resource. The door's alarm is its own native puzzle, not a ChainedPuzzleDataBlock a plan names, and no alarm resource provider exists in this runtime; the port is declared optional by the contract and a supplied value is refused by name instead of starting the door's own alarm under a different name.

the catalog declares an `alarm_handle` effect handle. RuntimeKernel mints handles only for its own timers (RuntimeKernel.Handles.cs CreateHandle has exactly one caller, the schedule path), so a command handler has no way to produce one; the port is declared optional and is never filled. This is the R-ABI batch C dependency (RuntimeModuleHandle.CreateEffectHandle / CreateLeaseHandle), not a claim that the alarm has no lifetime.

nativeEntries.meaning: key_policy=specific. The write exists and is implemented in Native/DoorActions.cs; what is missing is its input.

key_policy=none. The member takes the prompt text a player is shown at the door; the catalog row declares no port for that text, and the installation carries no standard 'locked' interaction-text constant (dump.cs has exactly one InteractionText_* constant and it belongs to a R7D2 mainframe event).

why: key_policy=specific needs a live native GateKeyItem instance. The catalog's `key` input is a forge.resource.item reference, and no resource provider resolves resource references to native instances in this runtime: RuntimeJson.ValidateValue has no `resource` branch and RuntimeKernel has no resource registry. R-ABI batch C (RuntimeModule.ResourceProviders, RuntimeQuerySession.TryResource) is the missing half.
key_policy=none needs the interaction text above; passing a valueless LocalizedText would show a player an empty prompt and is refused instead (Native/DoorActions.cs LockTextUnusable).
key_policy=any has no native meaning: the two lock setups take a concrete key item or a concrete prompt, and nothing takes 'any key'.
The catalog also declares a `lock` lease handle output; the runtime mints no provider handle yet (same batch C dependency as alarm_handle).
notImplemented.reshapeSuggestion: Either give the row a prompt-text input (making `none` carriable) and wire `key` through the resource registry once batch C lands, or drop the row's `any` member and keep `specific`/`none` only. Native/DoorActions.cs already implements both writes, so the reshape is an input-side change.

why: No honest native entry. The only candidate is LG_SecurityDoor::AttemptOpenCloseInteraction(System.Boolean) with onlyUnlock=true, whose parameter name is the entire evidence for its meaning, and LG_SecurityDoor::UseChainedPuzzleOrUnlock(SNet_Player) needs a player at the door and is the interaction path, not an unlock request.

The catalog's input is a `locks` lease handle produced by door_lock, and no provider can mint a lease handle today, so a required `locks` port would also make every unlock step unloadable (the action recipient validator refuses an optional recipient input).

Direct field writes to m_lockedWithNoKey / m_gateKeyItemNeeded with a recomputed lock state would not go through a native replicated entry, which Native/DoorActions.cs and the project's own rule refuse.
notImplemented.reshapeSuggestion: Delete the row, or reshape it onto the interaction entry once its onlyUnlock semantics is proven in game (see gameVerificationPlan). Do not implement it as a Forge-side field write.

nativeEntries.meaning: the addressed door kind's own damage entry is the folded empty body (`ret 0`), so a request against an addressable door is a request nothing carries out.
the damageable door kind's entry has a real body, but no weak door has an address in this provider's grammar.

why: The address grammar (MapObjectDoorAddress) names exactly one door per zone: its `security` entrance gate, which is an LG_SecurityDoor. Ruling 65's address layer produces no weak door, no node door and no decorative door, and LG_WeakDoor carries no zone identity to build one from.
So the row's recipient kind and its only damageable native kind do not intersect today: the honest answer is a missing stable identity, not a damage implementation.

Native/DoorActions.Damage keeps the refusal and its codes (door-not-damageable, door-damage-type-unknown, door-source-position-unusable) as the layer that would be bound if a weak-door address is ever defined; the row itself is not registered, so a plan that pins the capability fails to resolve a binding instead of receiving a row that can never commit.
notImplemented.reshapeSuggestion: Either delete the row, or extend the address grammar with a weak-door key (a second door key per zone) before the row is bound.

derivedFacts: A door's own alarm is reachable from the address layer without any new identity: LG_SecurityDoor_Locks.ChainedPuzzleToSolve is read off the same instance DoorObservation already resolves, so the alarm row needs no second door table.

MasterActivate/MasterDeactivate being public in interop while private in dump.cs is a general fact about this installation's interop build, not specific to the alarm row: any native member the dump calls private must be checked against the interop assembly before it is called.
unproven: Whether MasterActivate on a door alarm actually raises the wave in a running session, and whether MasterDeactivate stops a wave already in progress (the call edges say it calls TriggerEnemyWave; no session was observed).

Which peer runs MasterActivate in a real session: the instance is a state-replicator provider (ChainedPuzzleStateChange's side basis), and the catalog says host, so this action is gated host-only, but no replication was observed.
Whether m_hasAlarm is true for every author-defined door alarm and false for every door scan; it is read by name only.
Whether AttemptOpenCloseInteraction's toggle can be raced by a second request between this layer's status read and its call.
Whether LG_SecurityDoor.AttemptDamage's empty body is a build artefact or an intentional no-op for security doors (its address is shared with 2102 other dump entries).
What Localization.LocalizedText a vanilla no-key door lock is set up with; no standard constant was found in the dump.
gameVerificationPlan: Load a level with an alarm security door and a logic plan wiring the alarm row; check that start raises the alarm wave and that a second start reports door-alarm-already-active without a second wave.
Check that stop clears an active alarm and that a stop on an inactive one reports door-alarm-not-active.
Check a scan-locked door (m_hasAlarm false) refuses with door-not-an-alarm.
Check a plan whose door reference was minted in an earlier world is refused with door-stale, and one whose door was replaced within the same world with door-identity-mismatch.
Check door_open's respect/force difference on a locked door, and that a second open on an open door reports door-already-open without closing it.
Check door_close crush/force refusals and that block+normal closes an open door.
